ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, given points A, B, and C are three points on circle $\odot O$, with radius $OC=2$, $\angle ABC=30^\circ$, the tangent line $AP$ intersects the extension line of $OC$ at point $P$, then how long is $AP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect OA.\\
$\because$ $\angle ABC=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOC=2\angle ABC=60^\circ$.\\
$\because$ PA is the tangent of circle $O$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle OAP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle OPA=30^\circ$.\\
$\because$ OA=OC=2,\\
$\therefore$ OP=2OA=4.\\
$\therefore$ $AP=\sqrt{OP^{2}-OA^{2}}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
Thus, $AP=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached geometry diagram shows a circle with center O. Points A, B, and C lie on the circle; C is on the right side of the circle with radius OC drawn horizontally. Point P is to the right of C on the same straight line as OC, so P lies on the extension of OC. A slanted line AP touches the circle at A, indicating AP is tangent at A. We connect OA for the argument. Reasoning: From the text, OC=2 and ∠ABC=30°. Since ∠ABC is an inscribed angle subtending arc AC, the corresponding central angle is ∠AOC=2∠ABC=60°. Because O, C, and P are collinear, ∠AOP=60°. Since AP is tangent at A, the radius OA is perpendicular to AP, so ∠OAP=90°. Thus triangle OAP has angles 60°, 90°, and 30°. Also OA=OC=2, and OA is the side opposite the 30° angle, so it is the short leg of a 30-60-90 triangle. Therefore AP, the long leg, is 2√3.
